---
title: "Writing from K3"
date: "2026-11-22"
description: "Back in Addenbrooke's hospital after a major heart operation in Papworth. And hopefully starting to blog again "
---

After near-emergency open-heart surgery at Papworth two and a half weeks ago, I am back across the road on the cardiac ward K3 in Addenbrooke's hospital. The surgery went very well according to the medics, and left me in remarkable little discomfort. I am back in Addenbrooke's for perhaps another four weeks because I still need six-times-a-day intravenous antibiotics to clear residual pockets of infection around the heart. One gets institutionalized so quickly that the prospect of a continuing long stay is quite manageable. 

And I'll say little more here -- too many further details would be tedious, except perhaps to others facing similar surgery, who are very welcome to get in touch.

But I will add this. When I signed the final consent form for surgery the night before, I was given an algorithmic estimate of the chances of various unwelcome outcomes. This time -- for it is the second time for valve-replacement surgery -- the chance of mortality was set pretty high, shall we say. How does one spend what might well be your last evening? In my case it was by listening intently to the wondrous Mitsuko Uchida playing some of the late Schubert piano music I have loved so much. What better? After which, very surprising to relate, I slept really soundly: how strangely unpredictable are the ways of the mind!

Post-operation, there was an amount of brain-fog. So for a while I wasn't up to doing much more than aimless browsing, listening to more music, streaming some (lighter!) opera and ballet from the Royal Opera House site, and re-reading Dorothy Sayers for the first time in decades. But suddenly a few days ago I found myself moved to read the long introduction to a new logic book (isn't that sad?): more about this soon. So I have had my big laptop brought back to hospital, meaning I can more easily write about this and that, and in particular can start occasionally posting here again. 

Onwards, then!
